root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `ParseIdentifier()` may advance `state->mangled_cur` by `length`, the parsed identifier length must be nonnegative.
root_cause_criterion.description: On the vulnerable original case, `ParseIdentifier()` reaches the protected `cursor_rewind` event even though `identifier_guard.length` is negative. On the fixed original case, the same negative length is guarded before any cursor advance. The closest source-grounded boundary mutation `identifier_length_zero_boundary` changes only the identifier-length token to a zero-length source name; that case genuinely executes `cursor_rewind` on the fixed side with the required predicate satisfied.

nodes.state: At the vulnerable pointer-update site, `state->mangled_cur` moves backward when the admitted identifier length is negative.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable original case satisfies `cursor_rewind.cursor_after < cursor_rewind.cursor_before`.

nodes.state: At the abi-tag sink probe, `ParseOneCharToken(state, 'B')` dereferences the same cursor value produced by the preceding rewind.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable original case satisfies `cursor_rewind.cursor_after == abi_tag_probe.probe_cursor`.

edges.relation: The same parsed identifier length observed at the incomplete guard is the length value immediately applied at the cursor-rewind statement.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable original case satisfies `identifier_guard.length == cursor_rewind.length`.

edges.relation: The pointer value written back to `state->mangled_cur` by the negative-length rewind is the same pointer value later probed by `ParseOneCharToken(state, 'B')` at the sink.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable original case satisfies `cursor_rewind.cursor_after == abi_tag_probe.probe_cursor`.
